scope: Recover full character snapshots and incremental item writes on the existing single-Map deployment. Functional persistence repair, not a publisher gameplay/balance rule.
implemented: Snapshot character/quest/inventory/hotkey/pet/companion/skill state on the batch thread. Append a checksummed versioned record with flushed temporary-file publication before clearing dirty flags or removing a logout session.

Journal incremental inventory and cabinet item upserts/deletes too. Clone item extension arrays. Flush pending direct changes before the full character snapshot so a prior item mutation cannot overtake its replacement.

Retain failed and ambiguously committed records, retry on timer, and acknowledge only after every save stage succeeds. Preserve the existing single-reader SQL lane and capture each operation boundary at enqueue time; never replay a future snapshot before an older queued non-journaled operation.

Recover before auction state/world registration/client listeners, and before reloading a logged-out character. Failed recovery denies admission; pending records forbid DB-free startup. A leased per-group/server directory prevents simultaneous writers and binds records to database identities without storing credentials.

Native hotkey verb 2 inserts are made replay-safe by transactional delete/insert of the absolute page, for both inserts and updates. Missing update rows are recreated. Failure on a later page rolls the transaction back.

Journaled SaveChar/SaveQuest/SaveInventory/SaveHotkey/SaveItemDirect calls require their procedures; absent procedures cannot silently acknowledge a durable record. Existing non-journaled callers keep their previous optional-procedure behavior.

Periodic, disconnect, shutdown, pre-companion-evolution, battle-queue, timed-bag and tournament snapshot calls share the same path. Shutdown now also excludes a temporary TournamentBackup character, matching the existing ordinary-save and incremental-save gate.

history_review.reason_for_change: The previous SaveCharData/SaveAllCharData paths cleared dirty quest/hotkey flags before SQL; FlushSaveAsync swallowed failures and discarded the only snapshot. Native hotkey insert verbs are not idempotent after ambiguous commit. Logout/SQL failure, durable replay, tuple/array fidelity and hotkey SQL rollback are reproduced in regression checks.

remaining: Real full MapService snapshot replay across native character/inventory/global timed items/pet/companion stages is now SQL-verified in a separate disposable instance, including killed-writer and late-failure recovery. See Gameforge/full-save-integrity.json. Full MapWorker/client logout/restart and distributed ownership acceptance remain open.

A journal is local to one Map/database ownership domain. Cross-Map main-owner fencing/coordination must be implemented and fault-tested before deploying recovery across independently writing Map servers; the current port already lacks complete cross-Map routing. Local file leases are not distributed character ownership.

This is a write-ahead retry mechanism for existing snapshot triggers, not one SQL transaction across the entire character or every gameplay event. Changes made before a snapshot/direct flush can still be lost on an abrupt crash. Other queued database actions keep their existing failure semantics; active-session gameplay during a DB outage is not certified.

SendPost character/mail child recovery now uses a SQL outbox, journaled issuance IDs and receipts; see Gameforge/quest-mail-recovery.json for SQL/process/file-fault evidence. External world-action continuations remain pending/blocked and distributed ownership is still open; no universal exactly-once gameplay claim.
RT_SOUL/TT_WARREGION compatibility evidence remains missing; no soul formula, conquest trigger or publisher balance value was invented.
